faqs.q: What is menopause?

faqs.q: What causes menopause?

faqs.q: What are the symptoms of menopause?

However, for others, it causes serious symptoms such as might sweats, hot flushes, vaginal dryness that can cause frequent infections, low mood and anxiety, a decreased sexual drive and problems with cognitions and focus. Whatever the symptoms may be, it is necessary to address them and get them resolved.

faqs.q: Does menopause cause osteoporosis?
faqs.a: Osteoporosis is associated with a deficiency of estrogen hormone. This causes excess bine resorption and leads to soft bones. Hence, osteoporosis is a very common condition observed after a menopause.

faqs.q: How long do the symptoms of Menopause Last?
faqs.a: The symptoms usually last for 4 years after the cessation of menstrual cycles. They can last even longer for some women.

faqs.q: How to treat symptoms of menopause?
faqs.a: If you are experiencing menopausal symptoms, you should see your GP. Most common treatment for menopause is a hormone replacement therapy (HRT). This therapy replaces the depleted hormones in the body and reverses the symptoms of menopause. Primary hormones that are given are estrogen and progesterone. These hormones are given both in combination or alone. This depends on the status of your uterus. Nevertheless, HRT is an effective treatment option for women who face severe symptoms of menopause.

The one and only indication for getting a vasectomy is childbirth control. If you’re a man, who along with this partner, have reached upon a decision to not have kids anymore, going through with a vasectomy is the best option for you.
It guarantees a 99% success rate, and is the safest, most convenient method to date. It is also cheaper and faster than female sterilization.

faqs.q: What Are the Preparations for The Procedure?
faqs.a: To begin with, before the vasectomy, you need to remove the hair from the front of your scrotum. We advise you to bring tight underwear or underpants as well. And, it would also be wise to arrange for a drive back home to avoid unnecessary pressure on your genital area.

faqs.q: Is Vasectomy Painful?
faqs.a: No, vasectomy is not painful. We will give you local or general anaesthesia to numb your body against pain. You might feel the piercing pain of the injection for sure, but other than that, you wouldn't feel anything.

faqs.q: Can you Still Ejaculate After Vasectomy?
faqs.a: Yes. Vasectomy doesn’t affect your ability to ejaculate. You will be able to ejaculate the way you did before, only with 0 sperms in your semen.

faqs.q: Are You Capable of Making Someone Pregnant After a Vasectomy?
faqs.a: Vasectomy promises a 99% success rate in the process of male sterilization. So, no – there are significantly fewer chances for you to make someone pregnant after getting a vasectomy.

faqs.q: What Happens to the Sperms? Where Do They Go?
faqs.a: Your testicles are responsible for manufacturing the sperms, and the vas deferens carries them to the urethra. In here, the sperms get mixed with the semen and are then ejaculated out of the body. However, after a vasectomy, your sperms are unable to reach the urethra. Hence, they die and are eventually absorbed by the body.

faqs.q: Does getting a Vasectomy Affect Your Sex Drive?
faqs.a: No, vasectomy does not affect your sex drive because you're still producing the male hormone, testosterone, in your testicles. Your testicles are responsible for manufacturing the sperms and testosterone, which are not affected during a vasectomy. Vasectomy means just severing the tubes responsible for carrying the sperms to the urethra.

intro: Peyronie's Disease is a condition which causes the penis to become curved in appearance due to the fibrous tissue becoming damaged - usually due to an injury or vigorous sexual intercourse. People with the disease may experience soft erections, lumps and pain which really impact the quality of life.

Men with the disease often find it very painful, especially when it comes to intercourse. This debilitating condition rarely goes away by itself, frequently becoming even worse if left untreated. The right treatment plan is critical for addressing this disease, which can be embarrassing for many people and complicated to treat. At our Edgbaston Clinic, we will instantly put you at ease during your private consultation and one of our experienced gynaecologists will recommend the best treatment plan. We have a range of the latest advanced methods to suit your personal condition and needs. These include Hyaluronic Acid Fillers, PRP, Ultrasound and Shockwave Treatment.

faqs.q: What causes Peyronie’s Disease?
faqs.a: Peyronie’s Disease is usually caused by trauma or injury to the penis, however some men do not recall an injury, and it could be due to age. Some people believe Peyronie’s Disease could be hereditary or due to environmental factors.

faqs.q: How do you spot Peyronie’s Disease?
faqs.a: Many men first experience lumps underneath the skin of the penis, which is then diagnosed as Peyronie’s Disease or an upward curve in the penis, along with pain. Excessive plaque accumulation can also shorten the penis and make it feel tight. Erectile dysfunction and pain during sexual intercourse are also key symptoms.

faqs.q: What happens if Peyronie’s disease is left untreated?
faqs.a: If left untreated, your symptoms may get worse such as a more curved appearance, more lumps forming and even less of an ability to achieve erections. Along with these symptoms which will affect your quality of life, you will experience increasing pain as the disease progresses. The disease rarely goes away on its own, so medical help is needed.

faqs.q: Will Peyronie’s Disease affect my fertility and sex life?
faqs.a: Peyronie’s Disease can not affect your fertility levels, but it can make sexual intercourse painful and alter your erections. Therefore, the disease can have a huge impact and the curved appearance can make it difficult for both you and your partner.

faqs.q: How long does Peyronie’s Disease last?
faqs.a: The disease is permanent, but there are many treatment options available to cure the symptoms you are experiencing.

faqs.q: Which treatment is best for me?
faqs.a: Our experienced gynaecologists will be able to put you at ease and assess your individual situation. They will be able to discuss your symptoms and determine whether you are in the acute or chronic phase of Peyronie’s Disease.

faqs.q: Can Lifestyle changes improve this condition?

faqs.q: What is Flexible Cystoscopy?
faqs.a: Flexible cystoscopy is a short minimal-invasive procedure to detect bladder and bladder associated problems. It involves passing a flexible tube (cystoscope) through the urethra into the bladder to visualize its internals. The tube is attached with a camera, the images from which are displayed on a screen. These visuals are used by experts to establish a diagnosis.

faqs.q: When do I need a Flexible Cystoscopy?
faqs.a: A flexible cystoscopy is indicated when you experience problems with your urination process. These may include pain and discomfort while urinating, blood in urine, frequent urinary tract infections and a highly irritable bladder. The underlying cause for these issues can be determined after an in-depth examination of the tract and bladder through cystoscopy.

faqs.q: How long does it take for a flexible cystoscopy?
faqs.a: It is a short procedure that is carried out in the outpatient department. It usually takes only a few minutes (as little as 5 to 10 minutes). A sterile fluid is run through the tube to stretch the bladder to obtain a better view of its lining.

faqs.q: Is flexible cystoscopy safe and reliable?
faqs.a: It is a safe procedure that allows direct inspection of the bladder and its lining epithelium. It is done to diagnose and treat a wide range of bladder problems. Not only that, but it also helps to remove small polyps and stones through the use of dedicated instruments.

faqs.q: What is done in a flexible cystoscopy?
faqs.a: Flexible cystoscopy is a short procedure. First, an anaesthetic jelly is passed into the urethra to make the procedure painless and comfortable. A cystoscope is then inserted through the urethra all the way up to the bladder to examine it. The urologists also pass sterile fluid through the cystoscope into the bladder to stretch it and obtain a better view. The urologists may also take bladder biopsies for any further investigations.

faqs.q: Is flexible cystoscopy painful?
faqs.a: This procedure is a short and safe procedure that is completely painless. It involves administering a local anaesthetic through the urethra which means you are fully awake during the procedure but do not experience any pain. The procedure ensures a fast recovery. Hence, you can resume your activities the very next day of the procedure.
